_ghiChu: SỔ ĐĂNG KÝ NGÔN NGỮ — nguồn duy nhất cho cả backend (config/ngonNgu.js) và frontend (frontend/src/lib/ngonNgu.js, alias @ngonNgu). Thêm ngôn ngữ: khai báo một mục ở đây; bật cho người học (hoatDong: true) khi đã có nội dung (bộ từ, kho ngữ pháp...). 'bi' không phải ngôn ngữ mà là chế độ bộ từ song ngữ Trung–Anh, giữ riêng.

phatAm.luuY: Mark word stress. Connected speech to look for: consonant-to-vowel linking (an apple), flap t/d between vowels (water, better), elision of t/d between consonants (next day), weak forms of function words (to, and, of, can), contractions, and reduced vowels (schwa). Common problems for Vietnamese speakers: final consonants dropped or unreleased, th, v/z/ʒ, consonant clusters, missing -s/-ed endings.

ngonNgu.goiYWhisper: 以下是普通话的句子，使用简体中文，并加上标点符号。

prompt.chiChuViet: Write only Chinese characters and Chinese punctuation: no pinyin, no English.

capDo.easy: HSK 2-3: common words, short simple sentences
capDo.medium: HSK 3-4: some common set phrases, a few longer sentences
capDo.hard: HSK 5: set phrases (成语) where natural, longer sentences

prompt.diemDocHieu: set phrases, measure words, aspect (了/过/着)

phatAm.luuY: Tones are the core: give each syllable its tone. Sound changes to look for: third-tone sandhi (你好 nǐ hǎo → ní hǎo), tone changes of 一 and 不, neutral tone, erhua (儿化). Common problems for Vietnamese speakers: zh/ch/sh vs z/c/s, j/q/x, the ü vowel, the 3rd tone, and the aspirated p/t/k/q/c/ch.

prompt.vietBang: natural Japanese (kanji with hiragana and katakana)
prompt.ghiChuChuViet: using standard kanji and kana, no furigana, no romaji
prompt.chiChuViet: Write only Japanese (kanji, hiragana, katakana) and Japanese punctuation: no furigana in brackets, no romaji, no English.

capDo.easy: JLPT N5-N4: common everyday words, short simple sentences in polite です/ます form
capDo.medium: JLPT N4-N3: some common expressions, a few longer sentences joined with て, から, けど
capDo.hard: JLPT N2: natural expressions, longer sentences with subordinate clauses

prompt.diemDocHieu: particles (は/が/を/に/で), verb forms and tense, politeness levels, omitted subjects

phatAm.chuan: hiragana reading followed by Hepburn romaji, e.g. "がっこう (gakkō)"
phatAm.luuY: Sound changes to look for: long vowels (おう, えい read as long vowels), small っ (doubled consonant with a short pause), ん before b/m/p sounding like m and before k/g like ng, devoiced i/u (です → des, ～ます → mas), particles は→wa, へ→e, を→o, and pitch accent (mark high/low for important words). Common problems for Vietnamese speakers: vowel length, っ pauses, つ (tsu), ふ (fu), and the r sound.

prompt.ghiChuChuViet: in Hangul only, no romanization, no hanja
prompt.chiChuViet: Write only Korean in Hangul with normal punctuation: no romanization, no hanja, no English.

capDo.easy: TOPIK 1-2: common everyday words, short simple sentences in polite 해요 form
capDo.medium: TOPIK 3: some common expressions, a few longer connected sentences
capDo.hard: TOPIK 4-5: natural expressions, longer sentences with clauses

prompt.diemDocHieu: particles (은/는, 이/가, 을/를), verb endings and tense, speech levels and honorifics

phatAm.chuan: Revised Romanization of Korean, plus the ACTUAL pronounced Hangul in square brackets when it differs from the spelling, e.g. "합니다 [함니다] hamnida"
phatAm.luuY: Sound changes are essential in Korean: liaison 연음 (음악 → [으막]), nasalization 비음화 (합니다 → [함니다], 국물 → [궁물]), tensification 경음화 (학교 → [학꾜]), aspiration 격음화 (좋다 → [조타]), palatalization 구개음화 (같이 → [가치]), and ㄹ changes. Common problems for Vietnamese speakers: plain vs tense vs aspirated consonants (ㄱ/ㄲ/ㅋ), ㅓ vs ㅗ, ㅡ, and final consonants (patchim).
